Sam (PMM): quick sync — we need a 48hr tactical sprint to tighten the competitive messaging for next week's webinar and update the field battlecard. focus: claims that survive probe questions and routing tweaks for inbound leads.
Priya (Growth): yes — webinar signups are trending, want crisp hooks vs cloud providers + infra vendors. can we A/B test two opening lines?
Maya (Field): from recent calls, reps want 1-sentence rebuttals for claims about cost and 'managed vs dedicated' tradeoffs. short bullets only.
Ben (Sales Ops): routing note — if webinar attendee company_size >= 1000 OR budget_est >= 200k, route to AE queue; else SDR. also tag with "benchmark-interested" if they click benchmark slide.
Jorge (Research): propose primary claim set:
- predictable latency SLOs at scale (quantified: p95 < 120ms on 2K rps in our bench)
- unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private (single API surface)
- cost controls: batching + KV caching = up to 4x token cost improvement for chat flows
Eve (Content): those numbers are great but we should soften to "customer-observed" language for public materials. field copy can be sharper.
Sam (PMM): agree. public launch lines vs rep scripts should differ. Public blog/webinar: "customer-observed p95 < 120ms at 2k rps". Field battlecard: "p95 < 120ms in our production run — ask for the benchmark deck"
Maya (Field): can we add 2 quick objection handlers?
Eve (Content): sure, drafts: 
- "Why not just use cloud provider endpoints?" -> "Cloud endpoints give access but not predictable economics — we provide deterministic capacity controls and routing policies that protect latency during spikes."
- "Isn't model ownership enough?" -> "Model choice is only part of the problem — serving determines latency, cost, and reliability at scale. we handle it for you across environments."
Priya (Growth): for the A/B test, two webinar openers: 
A) "How to get predictable, production-grade LLM responses without rebuilding infra"
B) "Cut token spend and stabilize latency: a practical playbook for LLM features"
Which one do we want for ads vs email?
Ben (Sales Ops): run A in ads, B in nurture emails. measure CTR -> signups -> MQL conversion. set experiment tag: "openerv2_test"
ops-bot: calendar event created by Sam: Webinar Messaging Sprint • 48h • starts 3901112230 • attendees: Sam, Priya, Ben, Jorge, Maya, Eve
Jorge (Research): quick ask — I can produce a 2-slide benchmark summary and a 1-page appendix with test harness details. I'll include sequence length distribution and model variants used.
Sam (PMM): perfect. deliverables:
- Jorge: 2-slide benchmark summary + appendix (due 3901112650)
- Eve: field-ready rebut bullets + 1pg battlecard update (due 3901112800)
- Priya: set up A/B ad/email test + tracking tags (due 3901112400)
- Ben: inbound routing rule change in SFDC and SDR playbook update (due 3901112900)
- Maya: rehearse 3 field lines for the webinar demo (due 3901113000)
Maya (Field): will do. can we also add a short prompt/eval to show quality parity? a single slide with prompt -> redwood vs cloud example.
Eve (Content): yes, but keep it anonymized. use synthetic data or opt-in customer example.
Priya (Growth): tagging plan for inbound: add tags [webinar_3901, benchmark_interested, openerA] as conditions. routing rule snippet for ops: ```if lead.source == "webinar" and lead.score > 75 then route=AE queue elif click_list includes "benchmark-slide" then add_tag benchmark_interested; route=SDR```
Ben (Sales Ops): I can push the SFDC rule. will coordinate with ops for automation.
Sam (PMM): decision: go with A for ads, B for nurture. fieldcard language: stronger claims with "ask for benchmark deck" CTA. keep all public phrasing as "customer-observed".
Maya (Field): +1. quick note — reps want an objection cheat sheet with exact one-liners. Eve can we keep 6 max?
Eve (Content): yes — I'll limit to 6 and add a "quick revert" for pricing pushbacks.
ops-bot: deployment note: s3://redwood-assets/benchmarks/webinar-390111 slides uploaded by Jorge at 3901112555
Sam (PMM): great. check-ins every 12h in this thread. let's move fast — 48h sprint. :rocket:
